title: Water and Waste — Vacuum Toilet Assembly — Install the Two Lip Interface Seal and the Low Force Latch
abstract: Replaces the bowl to shroud interface seal, its retaining bracket and the toilet latch assembly, removing the odour path that opens as the delivered seal takes a permanent set.

sections.planning_reason: Lavatory odour was the largest single cabin dissatisfaction item for three operators, at about four complaints per thousand passengers on long sectors. Teardown of twelve returned assemblies showed the interface seal taking a permanent set after roughly eighteen months of servicing cycles, leaving a gap of up to one and a half millimetres at the aft edge that the flush cycle draws air through in the wrong direction. Replacing the seal alone does not hold, because the latch has to be over-centred to compress it.
sections.description: This bulletin replaces the interface seal with a two lip design in a different compound, fits the revised partition bracket that carries the seal groove, and replaces the latch assembly with the lower force variant. The harness behind the shroud is re-tied with the current cable tie standard so that it no longer bears on the new bracket. The waste tank, drain line and flush control are unchanged.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Isolate the lavatory and put it out of service, then remove the shroud. Remove the latch assembly and the existing seal and clean the interface faces. Install the revised partition bracket on the existing holes, fit the two lip seal into the bracket groove and seat it as described. Install the low force latch and set the closing force with the gauge supplied in the kit. Re-tie the harness clear of the bracket with the supplied cable ties. Refit the shroud, do the flush and seat check in AMM-M-38-30-11-800-039-A and confirm the seating gap is within limits at four points. Repeat for each lavatory and make the records entry.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to MERIDIAN-42 and MERIDIAN-46 aircraft between MSN M00069 and M00272, excluding MSN M00219, which was delivered with the post modification standard. All lavatory positions on an aircraft must be embodied at the same visit, because the servicing task is written against a single seat and latch standard across the cabin.
sections.material_note: Kit is per aircraft and covers every lavatory, with one seal, bracket and latch per position plus the cable tie set. Removed latches are returned for credit. Seals have a twenty-four month shelf life and must not be fitted beyond it.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience, normally at an A check.
